articleTitle: Detection and sequence of collecting loose oil palm fruit using deep learning technique
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper uses YOLOv7 to detect and collect loose palm fruits with an autonomous harvesting robot. YOLOv7 was chosen due to its high accuracy and real-time detection capability. Data from high-resolution cameras in oil palm plantations are annotated to create a robust training set. Key hyperparameters such as Anchor, Learning Rate, and Weight Decay are fine-tuned to see which performs well in object detection. The robot uses YOLOv7 to detect fruits, prioritizing picking based on the coordinates of the bounding box. Hyperparameter set A excels in detection accuracy and precision, while set B is slightly better in bounding box prediction. MAP50 is 0.866 and 0.823 for sets A and B, respectively. The optimized model significantly improves the efficiency of the robot in real-time harvesting.

articleTitle: A comparison of binary and non-binary codes approaches on the reliability and security performance of full-duplex transmission
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of binary and non-binary coding approaches on the security performance of Full-Duplex transmission systems. In the context of modern communication networks, where data integrity and confidentiality are paramount, the study evaluates the effectiveness of Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes in both binary and non-binary formats. By employing security gap and Bit Error Rate (BER) as key performance indicators, we explore how each coding scheme impacts the resilience of Full-Duplex transmissions against potential eavesdropping and self-interference. Our findings indicate that while binary LDPC codes exhibit certain advantages in terms of lower complexity and implementation ease, non-binary LDPC codes demonstrate superior performance in mitigating bit errors and enhancing security under adverse conditions especially in high order of modulation. This comparative study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the trade-offs involved in selecting binary versus non-binary LDPC codes for secure and efficient Full-Duplex communication systems and offers insights into optimizing data communication protocols for improved reliability and security performance.

articleTitle: CMDR: an artificial intelligence card game application using prominent Philippine historical figures
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Trading card games have long been a popular form of entertainment in the Philippines, attracting people of every demographic and age. Due to their versatility, card games have drawn increased attention and have taken on new significance in settings outside of traditional play, such as e-sports and education. This project attempts to capitalise on this popularity by developing an AI card game application that employs neural networks and is meant to be both amusing and informative. The major goal was to provide an entertaining and engaging platform where people of all ages may investigate and learn about Philippine history via engaging activities. By incorporating well-known historical figures and occasions from Filipino history into the card game format, the program aims to improve historical accessibility and enjoyment. This AI-driven application's usage of neural networks enables dynamic gaming that adjusts to the player's skill level, making it more demanding and individualised. This raises user engagement and offers a way to investigate how artificial intelligence and gaming connect with education. Furthermore, this project's research and development will serve as a model for enhancing AI capabilities and card game gaming mechanics generally. This study gives important insights into viable tactics for combining AI with card games, particularly in educational contexts.

articleTitle: Power transformer health index (HI) prediction using Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Power transformers are critical assets in electrical power systems, and ensuring their reliability and longevity is paramount to maintaining the stability of power grids. One of the most significant threats to transformer health is internal degradation, which can manifest through electrical and thermal stresses. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is a widely accepted method for diagnosing transformer health by detecting specific gases dissolved in the transformer oil. These gases, including hydrogen, methane, ethylene, and others, are by-products of insulation breakdown and oil degradation, which occur due to faults like partial discharge, arcing, and overheating. While traditional methods for interpreting DGA data, such as the Rogers Ratio, Duval Triangle, and Key Gas Method, have been valuable, they often rely on fixed thresholds or expert judgment, which can limit their accuracy and scalability. Recent advancements in machine learning (ML) offer a promising alternative by enabling data-driven approaches that can identify complex patterns and relationships within DGA features. Machine learning models can learn from historical data, providing more accurate and timely predictions of transformer health and fault conditions. This paper presents an ML approach for power transformer health assessment, employing the Kolmogorov- Arnold Network(KAN) model. The study leverages DGA data to train and evaluate the models, aiming to enhance accuracy in fault detection. KAN is used to capture the non-linear relationship and complexity within the DGA data, while Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) serves as a baseline for comparison. The simulation results show the KAN model with 3 layers (and a single univariate layer), with an RMSE of 0.0011 andR2 of 1.000 in independently reserved test data. This result significantly outperforms the MLP and demonstrates a superior ability to handle nonlinearities and reduce prediction error.

articleTitle: Air pollution prediction and classification with a hybrid ANN-LSTM model in modern cities: a comparative study
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Urban environments and industrial activities contribute to air pollution, a critical issue with significant health impacts. This study focuses on air pollution in urban and industrial environments and proposes a hybrid model to predict and classify air pollution levels. The model combines Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to analyze air quality data’s complex and time-dependent nature effectively. A comprehensive dataset of over 60,000 samples of air pollutants, including particulate matter (PM2.5), was collected to evaluate the hybrid model. These pollutants were carefully selected as key indicators of air quality. The hybrid model’s result was compared to various models such as Linear Regressions, Random Forests, Decision Trees, ANNs, and LSTMs. The results showed that the hybrid ANN-LSTM model demonstrated better performance compared to the other models, in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy of 94.87%. It also had the lowest prediction errors across MSE, RMSE, and MAE, as well as the highest R2 value and the lowest MAPE, indicating a good performance in forecasting air quality. This hybrid approach to air quality prediction and classification has the potential to significantly improve the management of air pollution and inform public health decisions.

articleTitle: Comparative performance of machine learning models for temperature prediction in vanadium redox flow batteries
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Vanadium Redox Flow Batteries (VRFB) are promising for large-scale energy storage due to their long life and environmental benefits. Accurate temperature prediction is key to optimizing VRFB performance and longevity. This study compares the performance of four machine learning models, i.e., 1D CNN, Particle Swarm Optimization - Support Vector Regressor (PSO-SVR), Decision Tree (DT), andK-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), using a publicly available dataset. Results show that KNN achieves the best results with test Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0424 (average) and testR2 of 0.9746 (average), demonstrating strong predictive accuracy. 1D CNN, however, shows poor generalization. These findings suggest that non-parametric models like KNN and DT are highly effective for VRFB temperature prediction.

articleTitle: Capacity prediction for Lithium-ion batteries using optimized long short-term memory networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Lithium-ion Batteries (LIBs) play an important role in many applications, such as electric vehicles. The prediction of the capacity of LIB is crucial in maintaining the performance of the batteries. Since data-driven methods outperform model-based methods in various ways, time series machine learning models have been used to predict the capacity. In this paper, we evaluate Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to predict the future capacity of two NASA LIB datasets. We compare two stochastic optimization algorithms, i.e., Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA), to optimize the hyperparameters of the LSTM. We also observe the effects of different train-test data split ratios, i.e, 50%-50% and 80%-20%. The results indicate that the 80%-20% ratio yields superior outcomes, with GA-LSTM outperforming PSO-LSTM, achieving a mean RMSE of 0.0130 for dataset B0005 and 0.0102 for dataset B0007.

articleTitle: A secure and automated student attendance tracking system utilizing NFC technologies for junior high school students at the UST
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of a secure and automated student attendance tracking system using Near Field Communication (NFC) technology for the students at the UST Junior High School. The system employs NFC-enabled ID cards, Arduino-based NFC readers, and a MariaDB database with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and role-based access control to ensure real-time attendance monitoring and data security. Developed using the Agile Software Methodology, the system integrates advanced network configurations, including VLANs, DHCP snooping, port security, and WPA3 encryption, to secure communication between NFC devices, a server, and faculty desktops. Features such as SMS notifications and automated PDF reports provide real-time updates to parents and streamline attendance management for faculty. The system was tested in a controlled laboratory environment for four Grade 9 sections, demonstrating its ability to enhance accuracy, administrative efficiency, and proactive student monitoring. Although implementation was conducted in few classes, the system is scalable to cover additional classrooms. This research highlights the potential of NFC-based systems in educational settings to improve operational efficiency and security while fostering better engagement between parents, faculty, and students.

articleTitle: Sodium-ion battery cycle life prediction using machine learning
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In this study, we explore the classification and prediction capabilities of three models—Genetic Programming (GP), Logistic Regression (LR), and the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN)—on the task of sodium-ion battery life prediction. By leveraging a dataset composed of multiple battery characteristics, we aim to determine the remaining power of sodium-ion batteries using these machine learning models. The KAN model, being a novel approach, demonstrates superior performance across various metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, when compared to the other two models. This highlights the potential of KAN as a robust model for complex classification tasks in the field of battery life prediction.

articleTitle: AUST: Ask - UST Chatbot for UST - ICT
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Effective communication is essential for understanding students' needs, and integrating artificial intelligence can enhance this interaction. This project aims to improve communication between students and administrative officials by developing features that enrich user experience. The researchers are committed to enhancing the platform by adding new functionalities to make offices more accessible and convenient for users seeking assistance with queries or issues. The primary goal of the applicat ion is to facilitate communication and provide individuals with the necessary information to address their concerns. To ensure a robust development process, the project employs the Iterative Waterfall Methodology, which allows for continuous feedback from earlier phases, enabling quick identification and resolution of issues before progressing to subsequent stages.

articleTitle: Delphi technique in identifying set of criteria for selection of maintenance strategy for large power user metering system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Selecting maintenance strategies is a crucial decision that requires a thorough understanding of their complexity. Multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) methods can help in this process by providing a structured approach. MCDA methods require alternatives and comparison criteria. The selection of maintenance strategies necessitates careful evaluation of criteria that significantly influence machine performance or the achievement of company objectives. This study aims to identify a set of criteria that will be evaluated in selecting a maintenance strategy for large power user metering system. The authors used the Delphi technique to identify the criteria. From criteria generated from literature and interviews, a panel of experts was surveyed using the Delphi technique to rate the importance of criteria in selecting maintenance strategy for large power user metering system.The study identified a set of criteria that can be grouped into safety, economic, feasibility, technical, organisational, and quality categories.

articleTitle: Exploration of explicit regularization terms in deep image prior
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Deep Image Prior (DIP) has emerged as an effective technique for various image restoration tasks, leveraging the implicit regularization properties of convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Despite its success, the role of explicit regularization in enhancing DIP remains underexplored. This paper investigates the significance of explicit regularization terms in DIP, with a focus on their impact on the quality and robustness of image restoration. We conduct a comprehensive analysis of different regularization techniques, including total variation (TV) and regularization by denoising (RED), to evaluate their influence on image denoising. Our experimental results demonstrate that explicit regularization significantly enhances DIP performance, offering improved consistency in denoising tasks. Furthermore, we examine the trade-offs between different regularization techniques regarding computational complexity and restoration quality. This study underscores the value of explicit regularization in enhancing DIP's effectiveness and provides practical guidelines for selecting suitable regularization strategies in image restoration applications. Notably, the experimental results indicate that incorporating explicit regularization variants of DIP, such as DIP-TV, can eliminate overfitting, resulting in a 2.7% increase in PSNR and a 1.8% increase in SSIM compared to the original DIP.

articleTitle: AOI-aware dynamic RL-based HAP-assisted UAV charging for data collection in WSNS
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The need for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) is becoming crucial in assisting wireless sensor networks (WSNs), such as collecting information data from sensor nodes, especially in challenging terrains, within their deadline requirement. The Age of Information (AoI) becomes then a key component in data collection, reflecting the freshness and importance of data which decreases with time if not collected. Moreover, UAVs are energy-limited and may need to be charged, which temporarily halts their data collection activities, leading to higher AoI. However, current AoI-aware studies often overlook the critical issue of UAVs' limited energy resources and assume that adequate charging infrastructure is readily available. This paper proposes an AoI-aware dynamic High Altitude Platform (HAP)-assisted UAV charging strategy for data collection in wireless sensor networks using Reinforcement Learning (RL). The UAVs' decision-making process is modeled and then enhanced through Q-learning, aiming at minimizing the overall AoI of sensors' data while considering the battery life of UAVs and extending their operational time. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach under various system parameters.

articleTitle: Development of an IoT -based fishpond water monitoring system using Arduino with enhanced depth measurement accuracy
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Water quality monitoring technology is an indispensable in fishery aquaculture. This paper is focuses on the deep pond aquaculture. The experimental study developed a fishpond monitoring system based on the Internet of Things. The system monitors the real-time water quality parameters such as depth, water temperature, air temperature, and humidity. Then the data is transmitted and stored through ONENET middleware and local database. Finally, the real-time monitoring results and alarms are displayed on a mobile application. The accuracy of depth measurement was tested in both clear and turbid water environments, with the average error rate of 2.84% and 4.09%, respectively. Moreover, Kalman filter-BP neural network algorithm is used to enhance predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Results shown that the root mean square error of the Kalman filter-BP neural network algorithm is optimized to 5.95%, compared to the standard BP neural network.

articleTitle: Film recommendation using scenario-based approach to solve the cold-start problem for new users
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Recommendation systems are a crucial component of modern internet activities. Typically, these systems rely on ratings given by users as the primary feature; however, this approach makes the system susceptible to the cold-start problem. To address this issue, the present study proposes using sentiment polarity as a feature in recommendation systems, especially in scenarios where user history information is unavailable. Subsequently, film ratings are used to evaluate the weighted score of sentiment polarity. For systems with access to user history data, a similarity-based algorithm is employed. In this study, the Fine-Tuned BERT + CNN model is utilised as a sentiment classifier. Additionally, Cosine Similarity is applied to calculate the semantic similar ity between two vectors—specifically, the query and the document—by leveraging BERT to capture the contextual meaning of each, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the outcomes.

articleTitle: Prediction of battery remaining useful life: an approach using Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are extensively used across various applications, including electronic gadgets, electric vehi- cles (EVs), and residential energy storage systems. Despite their higher upfront costs, LIBs have become the go-to energy storage option, surpassing traditional technologies like lead-acid and flow batteries. This dominance is attributed to their notable characteristics, such as high energy density, extended lifespan, fast-charging capabilities, and minimal self-discharge, making them crucial for energy storage systems (ESS) in both commercial and industrial sectors. However, degradation of LIBs over time are due to two factors : 1) calendar ageing (results in a slow loss of capacity), and 2) cycling ageing, (which occurs from repeated charge and discharge cycles). Factors that affect these process includes extreme temperatures, high charge/discharge currents, and operation at extreme states of charge can accelerate this degradation. Due to this reason, it is imperative to find the remaining useful life of the battery as a preventive maintenance approach. The ammount of research in this area largely focuses on the deployment of various machine learning models. Recently, the machine learning community has revisited Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KAN), positioning them as a competitive alternative to traditional feed-forward neural networks that use activation functions like ReLU and sigmoid. KAN is now being applied across various fields. In this study, it is used to predict the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of batteries. The findings reveal that KAN outperforms several models, including support vector machines (SVM), linear regression, and feed-forward neural networks, achieving an R2 value of 0.983.

articleTitle: Hybrid feature optimization – machine learning approach for predicting particulate matter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Dust storms in arid regions, particularly in the Middle East and UAE, carry substantial particulate matter (PM) over large distances, posing health risks, environmental concerns, and economic challenges. Predicting PM concentrations from dust storms is essential for public health and environmental stability. This study aims to introduce a hybrid feature optimization– machine learning (FO-ML) framework that leverages spatially distributed climatic data, including temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, wind direction, and wind speed. Data was collected from the Fujairah Research Center and optimized through a sequence of FO preprocessing steps, including normalization, feature selection using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and analysis with Pearson’s correlation matrix. The predictive ML model was developed using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN), optimized via grid search over the number of hidden layers and neurons. The best-performing configuration for PM2.5 achieved an R² of 0.90, an RMSE of 0.02, and a minimum prediction time of 19.1 seconds; for PM10, R² of 0.88, RMSE of 0.02, and 18.6 seconds. This setup used hidden layers with up to 100 neurons and ReLU activation. This research advances PM predictions, providing a tool for public health, environmental management, and policy decisions to mitigate PM impacts on ecosystems in affected regions.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of asymmetric multicore processors using ARM big.LITTLE architecture in MRI imaging reconstruction
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: MRI image reconstruction is a crucial process in medical diagnosis that requires high accuracy and computational efficiency. This research uses ARM big.LITTLE architecture on Orange Pi 5 device to improve the efficiency of MRI image reconstruction with Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT) algorithm. The k-space data of 512x512, 1024x1024, and 2048x2048 are tested in serial (big_CPU and LITTLE_CPU) and parallel (big_CPU, LITTLE_CPU with 4 threads, and hybrid bigLITTLE and LITTLEbig up to 8 threads) scenarios. Results show that big_CPU with 4 threads is optimal for 512x512 k-space, bigLITTLE with 8 threads is best for 1024x1024 k-space, and LITTLEbig with 8 threads is most efficient for 2048x2048 k-space, with speed-ups reaching 3,93 times. The hybrid configuration proved superior for medium to large data processing, while big_CPU remains ideal for small data. This research confirms the potential of the ARM-based AMP architecture.LITTLE in optimizing MRI image reconstruction, providing a balance between high performance and energy efficiency for medical applications.

articleTitle: Counting tilapia fingerlings using mask R-CNN
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This research develops a Mask R-CNN model with a ResNet-101 backbone to count tilapia fingerlings in overlapping conditions. The method is designed to address the limitations of manual counting, which is time-consuming and prone to human error in the fisheries industry. The dataset consists of 4,520 images of 2-3 cm tilapia fish fry taken in a fish farming environment. The process includes data collection, preprocessing, labelling, augmentation, and dataset division. The model is trained using various epochs, with the best performance achieved at the 300th epoch, resulting in a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.916 on the training data and 0.819 on the validation data. The evaluation demonstrates the model's ability to count tilapia fish fry by utilising bounding box analysis and Intersection over Union (IoU) to distinguish overlapping fish fry. The research findings show the potential of using computer vision technology to improve tilapia fish farming management and support sustainable aquaculture development.

articleTitle: Developing an English-to-Indonesian speech-to-text as a foundation for Sasak language translation using the mBART algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The advancement of speech-to-text technology has revolutionized data processing, enabling direct voice input, accelerating data entry, and supporting applications like auto-subtitling. However, challenges in translation accuracy persist, particularly for large datasets and regional languages. This study introduces an mBART-based translation model to convert English speech into Sasak text, effectively addressing dialectal variations. The model incorporates non-standard Indonesian as an intermediary, producing more natural and contextually accurate Sasak translations. Evaluated using the BLEU metric, the fine-tuned model achieved a score of 79.78 compared to 47.99 for the standard model, while the implementation of the CA-FIT Translation framework further improved performance, increasing BLEU scores from 48.79 to 64.99. These results highlight the effectiveness of fine-tuning and advanced frameworks in improving translation quality and preserving regional languages, supporting the development of more accurate multilingual speech-to-text technology.

articleTitle: Unmanned aerial vehicle localisation using RSSI-based trilateration
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) utilise the Global Positioning System (GPS) for navigation. Nevertheless, it is susceptible to obstruction and jamming threats. This paper investigates LoRa (Long Range) technology to create a redundant UAV localisation system, addressing the challenges of GPS dependency and vulnerability to signal disruptions. The system operates at 915 MHz, utilising Arduino and LoRa transceivers for Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) -based trilateration. LoRa provides an operational radius of up to 20 km in line of sight, providing GPS-free UAV navigation. Real-time monitoring and analyses have been performed via MATLAB and the IoT-based cloud platform, ThingSpeak. The experiment demonstrated that UAV localisation can be performed in line-of-sight (LoS) and Non-line-of-sight (NLoS) environments. The findings suggest that the path loss exponents of 3.2 and 3.4 were suitable for the area in which the experiment was conducted. LoRa’s exceptional capabilities such as its low power, long range and geolocation, help address the urgent demand for reliability in military, civilian surveillance and disaster response contexts. Future research is necessary to develop a complete UAV localisation system that utilises trilateration and LoRa technology. Further work can include testing with different antennas, testing in different environments and producing a real-time monitoring application.

articleTitle: Laser-induced graphene for moisture and micro-volume liquid sensing
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Fiber-reinforced composites have gained widespread adoption across various industries, including aerospace, automotive, and construction for decades. The growing necessity for monitoring environmental conditions during the storage and service life o f these materials has garnered scientific interest, especially in identifying exposure to harmful liquids that could compromise their structural integrity. Carbon-based sensors provide a unique ability for integration as sensing elements inside composite matrices, presenting an innovative path for multifunctional smart composites. This study presents the fabrication of laser -induced graphene on the surface of resin-infused brown paper, enabling seamless integration into composite structures. The LIG sensor exhibits excellent conductivity of approximately 1.6 kΩ, enabling it to monitor moisture absorption and identify hazardous liquids. LIG produced directly on the surface of composite materials has demonstrated its potential as a cost-effective detector for solvent leakages or moisture uptake in a composite structure, which can serve as a warning system for material degradation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Addax-based deep fuzzy clustering for face mask detection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Respiratory illness Diseases transmitted by droplets highlighted the necessity of face masks. The traditional methods to ensure mask usage faced challenges like the environment, partial masks, low-resolution, real-time processing, and human error, which hinder accuracy and efficiency dynamically. To handle these challenges, efficient automated mask detection systems are required in real-time across various environments. This work develops such an innovative model named Adaptive Addax Optimization Algorithm enabled Deep Fuzzy Clustering (Adaptive AOA_DFC). In this method, preprocessing is done using a Gaussian filter then undergoes Region of Interest (RoI) extraction to isolate the face region. Subsequently, the mask detection is performed using Deep Fuzzy Clustering (DFC) further trained through the proposed Adaptive AOA method. This algorithm is obtained by integrating the Addax Optimization Algorithm (AOA) with an adaptive mechanism to enhance detection accuracy. The performance evaluation metrics are Accuracy, Dice coefficient, and Jaccard coefficient, which yield the values of 92.39%, 0.950, and 0.951, respectively.

articleTitle: Passive-active crosstalk beyond low-frequency breakdown in mathematical-physical models of liquid crystal phase shifters at low-frequency applications
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: While most of the liquid crystal-based configurable and reconfigurable devices nowadays were designed to operate at the high-frequency microwave, millimetre-wave and optical wavelengths, there is a scarce of discussion on their feasibility at transmitting the low-frequency (LF) spectrum (low-data-rate but featuring lower attenuation and longer-range communication or detection). This work identifies a crosstalk vulnerability between the LF transmission signal and the LC-driving bias field for the first time. Furthermore, we comparatively quantify diverse line length requirements spanning the spectrum from 1 Hz to 100 GHz for the same LC coaxial phase shifters but fabricated by two different strategies, one with the conventional alignment agent-rubbing process (technically demanding, time-consuming, and costly), the other one featuring rubbing-free at the cost of a reduced tuning range of permittivity per unit length (i.e., requesting a larger physical size for 360° shifting to feed a phased array antenna).

articleTitle: Wind energy forecasts with supervised machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: United Nations set clean and affordable energy (7<sup>th</sup>) sustainable development goals. Among renewables, wind energy requires frequent observations. Due to limited finance in developing countries like Bangladesh, accurate and wide observations are one of the major challenges in operation and maintenance for energy harvests. Thus, this paper developed energy forecast models with supervised machine learning (ML) algorithms: support vector regressor (SVR) and random forest (RF) and compared with linear regression (LR) model. With global wind atlas (GWA) datasets (heights: 10 to 200m), training and testing performed with SVR, RF, and LR models. Model performances evaluated with Pearson correlation, coefficient of determinations, mean absolute percentage (MAPE), and root mean square errors (RMSE). During training and testing, ML estimations outperformed LR model as MAPE indicated ≤15% and ≥50% respectively for global and local-scale datasets. For an agricultural land with limited observations, ML predictions were performed for Bogura city with NASA-POWER dataset representing an MAPE of 4.84% (SVR) and 0.91% (RF). At Bogura on average, the final output showed annual energy production of 189 Kilowatt where probability for wind speeds about 70% (3 to 6 m/s at 50m). In conclusion, ML model accuracy is efficient for successful energy operations in Bangladesh and other developing countries with limited observations.

articleTitle: Enhancement and implementation of network infrastructure and security of general Miguel Malvar elementary school
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study redesigned and partially implemented a secure and scalable network infrastructure for General Miguel Malvar Elementary School (GMMES) to address limited coverage and security vulnerabilities in the existing system. Using the Network Development Life Cycle (NDLC), the researchers integrated VLAN segmentation, dual-WAN redundancy, a Windows Server 2019 file server, and a captive portal for user authentication. Partial implementation improved wireless coverage and security on the second floor, while full deployment was simulated in a controlled environment. Performance tests confirmed reduced latency, improved bandwidth, and enhanced wireless connectivity, validated through heat map analysis and user feedback. The study demonstrates a practical approach to modernizing network infrastructure in resource-constrained educational institutions, offering a scalable model for broader implementation.

articleTitle: Enhancing stroke detection in brain CT images with residual attention networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Stroke is becoming one of the most common diseases in modern society. Stroke caught in the early phase has a higher potential for recovery as it can be treated before the worsening of the patient’s condition. Detection through brain CT images with deep learning has a favorable impact. Residual Attention Network (RAN) architecture is proposed to perform stroke detection. RAN builds upon the regular ResNet architecture by incorporating an attention layer within each residual block to extract meaningful information. RAN combines the advantages of residual connections and attention mechanisms. RAN is able to prevent vanishing gradient problem while focusing on the most important features. RAN yields an accuracy of 96.12% surpassing the regular ResNet with an accuracy of 94.40%. RAN shows great potential, especially in fields that require high accuracy and efficient feature extraction. This paper explores the effectiveness of Residual Attention Networks and their potential applications in areas requiring robust and accurate feature extraction.

articleTitle: Smart pet micturition behavior corrector: utilization of computer vision for pet urinary activity detection, with adaptive deterrence, and progress monitoring
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Pet owners face challenges with managing their pets’ urination behavior, particularly when they are unable to consistently monitor and manually deter urination in unwanted areas in their homes. The study aimed to aid with the responsibilities of pet ownership, specifically in managing their pets’ urinary activity even without owner intervention. The objective was to develop a system that would benefit not only individual pet owners but also the majority of the pet care community facing similar challenges.This study developed a Smart Pet Micturition Behavior Corrector system that utilizes computer vision technology for the detection of pet urinary activity along with adaptive audio deterrence features and progress monitoring capabilities. The system employs a customtrained object detection model in YOLOv8 for real-time identification of pet urination events and triggering adaptive audio alerts through an ESP32-controlled Bluetooth speaker. The model achieved detection accuracy with 76% precision and 77% recall rates, and mAP@0.50 of 77% through 270 epochs of training. An assessment was conducted using the ISO 25010:2023 quality model, with feedback collected from 60 pet owners. The results demonstrated strong performance across key attributes. Functional Suitability received a score of 4.62 (Very Satisfied), while Interaction Capability achieved a score of 4.45 (Satisfied), and Reliability received a score of 4.44 (Satisfied). The overall system rating of 4.45 (Satisfied) indicates that the implementation of the system was a success.

articleTitle: ABCiFY: enhancing alphabet learning through image classification using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Traditional teaching methods, such as flashcards are often not enough to make teaching and studying of Alphabets engaging for children. The study presents an innovative system website called 'ABCIFY', which is designed for alphabet image classification using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), among children aged three to six. It enables children to capture common objects using their smartphones which reinforces children to engage in alphabet learning while at the same time familiarizing items in indoor environments (house and school)—for visual and kinesthetic learning. The web application features a Text-to-Speech function to support auditory learning, improving children’s pronunciation of letters. Additionally, it features an Interactive Quiz to evaluate and assist with children’s Alphabet recognition. The evaluation proceeded using ISO 25010, which determines and confirms the accuracy of the Image Classification in identifying objects and prompting responses, as well as the text-to-speech function for pronunciation and interactive quiz. The CNN model accuracy, on the other hand, demonstrated an 85% accuracy in image classification. To conclude, ‘ABCiFY’ reinforces a new approach of learning the alphabet in a more interactive and engaging way using Image Classification. Future enhancements of the study in terms of accuracy and functionality are essential for the improvement of the system.

articleTitle: Wind farm sensor fault diagnosis using artificial intelligence and wavelet transform
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: A methodology for the diagnosis of sensor faults in wind farms is introduced. Simulations are performed using a multi- domain model that integrates mechanical, electromagnetic, electronic control, and power grid components. The prevalent issue of intermittent sensor failures is addressed. The discrete wavelet transform is employed for feature extraction. The transient signals are processed effectively. Various wavelet families are evaluated to identify optimal candidates for fault diagnosis. Additionally, the methodology integrates three machine learning classifiers, achieving accuracy rates consistently exceeding 99%. The outcomes demonstrate the advantages of this approach in terms of enhanced accuracy. This research represents a significant advancement in sensor fault diagnosis, contributing valuable insights for the operation and maintenance of renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Integration of analytic hierarchy process and K-nearest neighbor methods in athlete selection in PDBI Banjarmasin City
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study presents a Decision Support System (DSS) that integrates the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and K-nearest neighbour (KNN) algorithms to enhance the athlete selection process for the Indonesian Drum Band Association (PDBI) in Banjarmasin. Traditional selection methods rely on subjective evaluations and often result in inconsistent outcomes. Based on this limitation, the AHP method is utilized to assign priority weights to various selection criteria, including physical ability, musical analysis, and leadership, ensuring a structured and objective decision-making process. Subsequently, the KNN algorithm classifies athletes based on their similarity to previous selections, using the AHP-weighted criteria to improve classification accuracy. The dataset comprises 56 athlete records with 11 normalized attributes to ensure consistent scaling across criteria. The system's performance is evaluated using a Confusion Matrix, achieving 94% accuracy, 98% precision, and 96% recall, thereby demonstrating the effectiveness and reliability of the integrated approach in selecting qualified athletes. This research highlights the potential of combining AHP and KNN to develop an objective, data-driven selection system that reduces biases and improves decision-making. Future work will involve testing the model with larger datasets and exploring alternative distance metrics in KNN for further optimization.

articleTitle: Potential criteria in multi-criteria evaluation of a substation site selection
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The paper presents the results of a review of the criteria for substation site selection. From the literature review conducted, the main criteria were environmental, technical, economic, and social. The environmental sub-criteria are topography and environmental factors affecting system reliability. The technical sub-criteria are site dimensions, incoming line feeders, geological and geotechnical characteristics of the soil, access roads, telecommunications infrastructure, and security. The economic sub-criteria are costs of construction, new feeder, access roads, telecommunications, mitigation strategies of suburban areas, and security respectively. The social sub-criteria are legal and regulatory compliance and socio-political conditions. The study gives an understanding of the criteria for site selection.

articleTitle: Enhancing audio signal segmentation for musical instruments with refined MFCC-based features
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of modified Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) features, incorporating Delta and Delta-Delta MFCCs, for classifying musical instruments—specifically drums, guitar, and keyboard. The modified MFCC approach was compared to the standard MFCC in terms of classification accuracy and instrument detection across five cross-validation folds. The results show that the modified MFCC outperforms the standard MFCC, achieving a classification accuracy of 95% compared to 86%, highlighting the importance of temporal features in distinguishing the unique audio patterns of each instrument. Additionally, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis was employed to identify dominant frequencies, revealing that drums dominate lower frequencies, guitars occupy mid-range frequencies, and keyboards cover a broad spectrum. Clustering of these dominant frequencies further confirmed their distinct spectral characteristics, validating the modified MFCC features as reliable indicators for instrument classification. These findings have significant implications for real-time applications in audio segmentation, music transcription, and AI-based music recognition, with potential use in music production, education, and other related fields.

articleTitle: Model compression using post-training dynamic range quantization for plant disease recognition
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study investigates model compression techniques for plant disease recognition using leaf images, focusing on reducing the computational burden of deployment on resource-constrained devices. Utilizing the PlantVillage dataset, the study trained and evaluated 11 prominent CNN architectures by employing a pocket algorithm for performance optimization. This study examines three training scenarios: random weight initialization, ImageNet pre-trained weights with trainable layers, and ImageNet pre-trained weights with non-trainable layers. The results demonstrated superior performance in scenarios with trainable layers, with the Xception model achieving the highest minimum accuracy. Subsequently, the study implements magnitude-based pruning using the PolynomialDecay strategy, successfully reducing the model size by 90% while maintaining comparable accuracy. Further compression was achieved through post-training dynamic range quantization, yielding a compression ratio exceeding 90% for most models without significant accuracy degradation. This study highlights the effectiveness of combining pruning and quantization to deploy accurate and efficient plant disease recognition models on devices with limited resources.

articleTitle: Estimation of state of charge in a solar charging system using artificial neural networks for lead-acid batteries
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Solar panel, as a renewable energy source, require batteries to store the generated energy. Continuous use of batteries can l ead to capacity reduction and performance decline. To address this issue, it is important to have a system that can estimate the State of Charge (SOC) of the battery to control the charging process and maintain optimal battery performance. This research develo ps an SOC estimation system for lead-acid batteries by applying the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) algorithm. The ANN method has several advantages, such as more efficient iteration processes, increased speed in parameter updates, and the ability to achieve convergence more quickly. Meanwhile, the ANN algorithm also offers advantages in ease of implementation and better interpretability. The SOC estimation results for a 48V, 12Ah lead-acid battery using the ANN algorithm show that the training phase reveals a compelling regression plot, demonstrating an impressive R value of 0.99979. The minuscule error rate in the prediction system unequivocally affirms the exceptional quality of this ANN model.

articleTitle: Real-time dual shutdown-enabled environmental monitoring system for cell sites
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Limitations in existing monitoring methods and delayed response times pose significant challenges within the telecommunications industry, particularly for cell site management. This study aims to address these issues by developing an advanced remote monitoring system that includes both manual and automatic shutdown capabilities for key environmental parameters, including water level, temperature, humidity, smoke, AC voltage, and current. Utilizing a Research and Development (R&D) approach, the system integrates GSM and IoT technologies to enable real-time data monitoring, threshold-based alarm notifications, and dual shutdown control. This modular, low-cost solution meets the demands of modern cell site infrastructure, offering enhanced accessibility and adaptability for efficient management and operation. The prototype system is constructed with an Arduino Mega, Ethernet Shield, GSM SIM 800l v2, DHT22, MQ-2, PZEM-004T, floaters, and the Blynk IoT platform. Rigorous testing—including unit, integration, and acceptance evaluations confirmed the system's functionality, efficiency, and effectiveness. Field engineers, directly engaged in operational testing, rated the prototype highly with weighted mean scores of 4.7 for functionality, 4.62 for efficiency, and 4.68 for effectiveness, as measured by a 5-point Likert scale.

articleTitle: Hybridising the future: recent progress on graphene and its hybrid for sensing, energy, and environmental applications based on VOSviewer analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The remarkable properties of graphene have attracted the attention of researchers since it can be applied in numerous application devices, including sensors, energy storage, and environmental sectors. Understanding the research trend and future potential of graphene has become an interesting topic to be explored. VOSviewer analysis was then used in this study to visualise and simplify the investigation. Based on the analysis, graphene research was observed to overlap with graphene oxide and have a close relationship with reduced graphene oxide. This result motivates further investigation into producing high-quality and scalable graphene. Moreover, sensors and energy storage have become the most explored applications. Nevertheless, research on photocatalytic, mechanical, and environmental sectors is still open to wide investigation.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of housing and electrode stack variations for a Lithium-ion battery cell
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are getting a lot of attention for energy storage to combat the effects of climate change. However, due to its diverse range of applications extending from small electronics equipment to large energy storage systems, its output requirements and limitations vary significantly. Many efforts are underway to increase the power and energy output of the cells without any significant compromise on their size and weight. This paper explores different housing sizes and types for an existing cell by Kokam that is initially enclosed in a pouch bag housing (118 x 97 x 8 mm). Furthermore, variations in the electrode stack are also investigated, including different active materials, thickness in electrode coating , and the total number of anode and cathode sheets. The Pareto front optimization tool is then utilized to pick a cell that gives the optimum results in terms of energy density. The parameter variation of the cells is done in the MATLAB application ISEA Cell and Pack Database (ICPD) created by the Institute of Power Electronics and Electrical Drives (ISEA) of RWTH Aachen University, which virtually builds up the physio-chemical model of the existing cells. This study concludes that the utilization of pouch bag housing, in conjunction with NCO and lithium metal as active materials, results in the high er gravimetric energy density thus enhancing the cell output from 139 Wh/kg to 216 Wh/kg.

articleTitle: Enhancing electrical performance of inkjet-printed flexible strain sensors through substrate surface coating and multiphysics simulation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Inkjet-printed piezoresistive sensors are gaining popularity due to process compatibility with flexible substrates and the possibility of rapid on-demand fabrication. However, several technical challenges are frequently encountered, such as the compatibility of commercial inks with non-standard substrate materials and the necessity to enhance sensor sensitivity for application-specific performance. This study introduces a novel approach for improving the sensitivity of Mitsubishi silver nanoparticle inks on non-standard substrates by utilizing a two-layer surface coating of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and potassium chloride (KCl). In this work, non-standard substrates such as standard paper, glossy inkjet paper, and polyimide were coated prior to silver nanoparticle ink deposition using an office inkjet printer. The baseline resistance of non-standard substrate was compared with the Mitsubishi special media. The baseline resistance measurements revealed the lowest values on Mitsubishi special media (4.74–6.43 Ω), while polyimide exhibited significantly higher resistance (426–894 Ω) with high variability (standard deviation of 170.10 Ω), indicating substrate-dependent conductive performance. Further multiphysics simulation studies investigating the influence of various design features on the sensitivity were performed. The results indicate that the unit cell of the meander pattern (Z-shape) enhances sensitivity of 96.1 in a confined area, making it an optimal design choice for strain sensor applications. Key findings revealed that both length and spacing width significantly influence sensor performance. The two-layer coating and design influence on sensitivity provides critical insights for enhancing the electrical conductivity and piezoresistivity.

articleTitle: Semantic search system for name of government work package using BERT
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study develops a semantic search system to improve query matching for government work packages using data from SIRUP (General Procurement Plan Information System) and KBLI 2020 (Indonesian Standard Industrial Classification). The existing SIRUP search system relies on keyword matching, which often fails to capture semantic relationships between queries and data. To address this, a two-stage approach was introduced: first, matching queries with main KBLI categories, and second, refining results by aligning queries with work package names under the identified category. The system leverages IndoBERT as its base model and incorporates fine-tuning to adapt to the procurement domain. While fine-tuning enhanced semantic relationships, it was insufficient to handle irrelevant data with high similarity scores. To overcome this, Triplet Loss was employed to optimize embeddings, improving the separation of relevant and irrelevant data. The evaluation involved 30 queries, with each query individually assessed for precision, recall, and F1 score. The system achieved an overall precision of 0.84, recall of 0.78, and F1 score of 0.80, demonstrating its ability to retrieve semantically relevant results effectively. This approach highlights the potential of semantic search to enhance query accuracy and relevance in the government procurement domain.

articleTitle: Exploring machine learning approaches for breast cancer detection: a comparative perspective
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Breast cancer, on the other hand, is the leading cause of death among women worldwide, necessitating early and timely diagnosis to reduce survival mortality rates. This traditionally relies on radiology tests such as mammography and, in some cases, biopsy, which have several clinical limitations in terms of invasiveness and a risk of false negatives/positives associated with the loss of precious time. This paper examines using machine learning techniques in improving diagnosis relating to breast cancer and reducing diagnostic errors. Using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset, several ML models including Decision Trees, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, and Neural Networks were evaluated. Performance metrics considered were accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Curve. The best neural network was MLP, outperforming other models and further showing how ML might offer accurate, non-invasive diagnostic alternatives. Further studies should be done to enable better real-world applications and clinical utility of such models.

articleTitle: Energy conservation potential for solar cooker constructed with 25-PPI copper foam layer as a porous absorber
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The thermal performance of two different models of box–style solar cookers was determined in natural environments. While the first solar cooker used copper absorber plates, the second box solar cooker used 25 PPI copper foam sheets. Solar cookers oriented to the south were erected in September 2023 in Baghdad, Iraq, with a latitude of 33.3 degrees north and 44. The heat absorber panel employed in the experiments is a copper metal foam with a pore density of 25 PPI, and the tilt angles used are 0°, 3°, 6° and 9°. The stagnation temperature of the device containing a 25 PPI copper foam absorber was found to be about 13 degrees higher than that of a box type solar cooker having a normal absorber plate. A 25 PPI copper foam absorber plate in a box-style solar cooker can save 31% more cooking time than that of a flat absorber plate. When the 25 PPI copper foam absorber panel is tilted at 6 degrees, the desired temperature of the internal air is reached. The cooking power equation of the cooker is well within the permissible limits, and that means one can safely use the cooker regularly for boiling water and cooking. The solar cooker with 25-PPI copper foam as a porous absorber can reduce energy conservation by 31% compared with a conventional solar cooker.

articleTitle: A learning mobile application and image recognition for children
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In an increasingly digital world, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, technology has become essential, with online classes emerging as the new norm. Many children aged 2 to 6 have had limited exposure to traditional classroom settings due to these changes. In response, an educational mobile application has been developed to help young children engage with various subjects and complete assessments using technology. The project aims to teach foundational skills such as spelling and pronunciation of shapes, letters, numbers, and colors while providing an enjoyable and interactive learning experience. This application is expected to significantly enhance children's understanding of these topics in a creative and entertaining environment. To ensure quality and efficiency in development, the Iterative Waterfall Methodology was employed, facilitating early feedback and error detection in the initial phases of the project before advancing to later stages. The application offers age-appropriate educational modules tailored for different age groups, ensuring content differentiation from basic shape and color recognition for 2-3-year-olds to advanced skills like addition and sentence reading for 4-5-year-olds. With integrated assessment activities, text-to-speech features, and image recognition capabilities, it effectively meets developmental goals and has been positively received by users.

articleTitle: Optimization of PSS parameters using surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms based on KAN
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This research presents an approach for tuning Power System Stabilizer (PSS) parameters using surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithms based on the recently proposed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN). Developed from the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, KAN replaces traditional weight parameters with spline-adjustable univariate functions, enhancing both accuracy and interpretability over conventional methods. The proposed approach has been tested on a ten-machine system, with performance comparisons made against various surrogate models based methods. Our preliminary numerical simulation results indicate that PSS parameters obtained by the proposed method are able to improve low-frequency oscillation damping. In addition, using surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithm accelerates the convergence towards optimal solutions compared to conventional parameter tuning methods.

articleTitle: Leak detection in water carrying pipe using a peak detector
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study is a continuation of previous work carried out here in the Chemical Engineering at the University of Bahrain. In the previous work, we first implemented what we called polarity correlation to determine the location where the leak occurs. However, the problem was the large amount of computation. The technique was modified to a more efficient one by implementing what was called zero crossing correlation, where computation was reduced extensively. Though both techniques contribute well in estimating the leak, it was thought that the computation could be reduced further by completely, eliminating the convolution. The idea behind the new technique is to place two hydrophones, one at each end of the pipe. When a leak occurs, it generates two signals, one upstream and one downstream. Depending on how far the leak from the transmitters is, there will be a delay between the two signals. Those signals generate a high peak with small secondary insignificant peaks. The time delay is generated as follows. A very fast 32-bit timer is set as a freerunning timer. When the first peak occurs on the first transmitter, the processor records the time. When the delayed peak occurs on the second transmitter, the processor records the second time. It then calculates the difference between the two. This difference represents the delay. Knowing the length of the pipe, as well as the geometry of the pipe and the flow velocity, the distance where the leak has occurred, is easily estimated.

articleTitle: Proactive DDoS attacks detection using deep learning techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In this study, present a comprehensive analysis of detecting Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks using advanced deep learning models, including a Deep Neural Network (DNN), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Long Short - Term Memory (LSTM) network. Leveraging the CICDDoS2019 dataset, we evaluate the performance of these models across several metrics, such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, log-loss, and ROC-AUC, to determine their efficacy in distinguishing DDoS attack traffic from normal traffic. The DNN model achieves an impressive accur acy of 98.31% and near-perfect precision and recall values, highlighting its robustness in capturing the characteristics of DDoS attacks. The CNN model, while effective, shows a slightly lower accuracy of 97.27%, indicating its limitations in processing c omplex sequential dependencies. The LSTM model, designed to learn from temporal patterns, demonstrates a solid performance with an accuracy of 96.78% and high recall, making it suitable for sequence-based detection scenarios. Furthermore, our analysis of log-loss values reveals that the LSTM model achieves the lowest value, indicating strong model confidence, while the ROC - AUC values emphasize the exceptional discriminative capabilities of all models, with the DNN model performing the best. These results underline the potential of deep learning techniques in enhancing DDoS attack detection, with each model offering distinct strengths depending on the data characteristics and detection requirements.
