articleTitle: Kelor: a mobile application for moringa powder quality detection using CNN ensemble transfer learning (case study: moringa powder)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Studies on powder quality detection using image processing have been widely conducted, particularly in the pharmaceutical field; however, the quality detection of moringa powder remains largely unexplored. Moringa powder, commonly used in products such as medicine, tea, and masks, is highly sensitive to sun and air exposure, which can significantly alter its quality. Therefore, reliable detection of moringa powder fit for consumption is crucial to ensure product safety and quality. This study investigates the application of a Convolution Neural Networks (CNN)-based transfer learning ensemble method for moringa powder quality detection, detailing aspects like datasets, pre-trained models, transfer learning concepts, ensemble techniques, and performance evaluation. In this research, ResNeSt101 and DenseNet121 were employed as pre-trained models within the transfer learning process. The evaluation results demonstrated that the ensemble transfer learning approach performed exceptionally well, achieving an AUC score of 0.868, with accuracies of 0.836 for ResNeSt101 and 0.838 for DenseNet121. These results highlight the effectiveness of this approach in detecting moringa powder suitable for consumption, underscoring the potential of the transfer learning ensemble method as a reliable solution for moringa powder quality detection.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a secure network infrastructure for enhanced digital learning at Mandaluyong high school
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of an enhanced network infrastructure for Mandaluyong High School, focusing on enhancement in terms of security, reliability, and scalability to support the increasing demands of modern educational environments. The study addresses limitations in the school’s previous network, including restricted coverage, frequent downtime, and security vulnerabilities. A dual-ISP configuration was introduced to ensure network redundancy, while centralized management through VLAN segmentation and access control was implemented to improve security and bandwidth allocation. The project follows the Network Development Life Cycle (NDLC) methodology, with the implementation covering 2 buildings (Gonzales Hall and Abalos Building). Key security measures, including Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), firewall protections, and WPA3 protocol, were applied to safeguard student and faculty data. Preliminary results from this deployment indicate improved connectivity, a 30% reduction in latency, and higher user satisfaction scores. This model demonstrates a scalable, secure approach to network infrastructure in educational settings, with potential implementation across additional buildings.

articleTitle: Towards formal modeling and verification of UML class diagrams using first-order logic and resolution
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Although Object Management Group (OMG) Unified Modeling Language (UML) introduced Object Constraint Language (OCL) to add formalism as constraints in its models, it still lacks formal semantics and verification. This paper proposes first- order logic for formal modeling UML class diagrams and resolution for verification. We introduce formal definition and semantics for classes, their attributes, and operations. In addition, we provide two case studies of class diagrams in which we prove inconsistencies can be detected in the classes and operations.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient job shop scheduling using hybrid mean-variance mapping optimization
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to address a 5-jobs-4-machines energy-efficient job shop scheduling problem using Hybrid Mean- Variance Mapping Optimization algorithm. Two case studies have been used to validate the algorithm effectiveness in minimizing the maximum makespan and the total energy consumption. A job's assignment is constrained to only one machine, and each machine can operate on a single job at a time, with no preemption. The obtained results are compared to previous studies that applied different metaheuristics on the same model problem. Hybrid Mean-Variance Mapping Optimization has demonstrated superior results compared to Genetic Algorithm and matched the results obtained by Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm in solving job shop scheduling problems with energy considerations in the manufacturing environment. The algorithm's simplicity and the fewer adjustable control parameters are distinct advantages over other algorithms.

articleTitle: Characterization of corrosion and wear for magnesium-based metallic glass
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper delves into the design and analysis of a Polyphase Decimation Filter (PDF) implemented using state -of-the-art semiconductor technologies, including 130nm, 32nm, 16nm MOSFETs, and 15nm Graphene Nanoribbon Field-Effect Transistors (GNRFETs). The primary objective of this research is to optimize the PDF's power consumption, delay, and power- delay product (PDP) for high-speed, low-power signal processing applications. The paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the power, delay, and PDP characteristics of the various internal components of the PDF, as well as the overall filter. Th e results demonstrate the potential of advanced semiconductor technologies, particularly GNRFETs, in significantly enhancing the performance of the PDF, making it a promising solution for demanding signal processing tasks.

articleTitle: Development of plum ripeness sorting system using colour sensors
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Sorting is an important post-harvest process that extends the shelf life and enhances their market value. At present, plum sorting plums in orchards is usually done manually which is inefficient, time consuming when dealing with large quantities. Moreover, manual sorting incurs high labour costs and is subject to variabilities due to differing individual judgement standards. To address these challenges, an automated sorting machine capable of rapidly detecting and categorizing plums based on colour is proposed. This machine aims to improve productivity by efficiently grouping fruits according to their ripeness. The system utilizes the TCS3200 colour sensor to classify plums into four categories: unripe, semi-ripe, fully ripe, and rotten. The sorting process is driven by a servo motor and controlled by STM32 and ESP32 microcontrollers.

articleTitle: SVM classifier optimisation for predicting anomalies in login data with SMOTE
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The global cyberattack increase underscores the importance of more robust cybersecurity measures, particularly in detecting account takeovers. These incidents occur when unauthorized parties access user accounts, potentially leading to financial losses, data breaches, and reputational damage. The primary challenge in detecting account takeovers lies in their similarity to legitimate network traffic, making them difficult to identify using traditional methods. This research proposes using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm with a linear kernel optimized through RandomizedSearchCV to detect anomalies in login data. The dataset includes attributes such as IP addresses, geographical locations, network providers, device types, login times, and indicators of suspicious activity. Preprocessing uses the Interquartile Range (IQR) to remove outliers and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to balance minority class data. This process ensures optimal data quality before further analysis. The research findings demonstrate that the SVM model achieves precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy of 96%, proving its effectiveness in detecting anomalies and handling imbalanced data.

articleTitle: Characterization of corrosion and wear for magnesium-based metallic glass
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The corrosion and wear behaviour of magnesium-based metallic glass (MgMG) was systematically investigated using a scanning Kelvin probe (SKP) and atomic force microscopy (AFM). The open circuit potential (OCP) of the MgMG exposed to a 0.1 M NaCl solution for 40 hr was about −412 mV vs. SHE. The scratch-induced wear of the MgMG generated by AFM scratching was apparently higher at the higher set-point voltage because the higher applied load resulted in the removal of more materials from its surface.

articleTitle: Boosting algorithms in breast cancer classification: accuracy and performance metrics analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent cancer among women all over the world, so its early detection is of great significance. Th e traditional methods of detection, while effective, are quite inaccurate. This research evaluates the performance of various boosting algorithms, including AdaBoost, CatBoost, Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting, LightGBM, XGBoost, and Gradient Boosting using the Breast Cancer Wisconsin Original dataset. Our methodology encompassed data exploration, pre- processing, model training, and analysis of results. Among them, the HistGradientBoost model proved to be one of the efficient ones with very high accuracy, precision, recall, and a well-balanced F1-score, besides its excellent AUC score. These results set a great clinical significance for the application of HistGradientBoost in the diagnosis of breast cancer. In addi tion, this dataset will be expanded, integrated with deep learning techniques, and hyperparameters will be optimized further to enhance the performance of models in the near future. This can provide valuable input to data scientists and medical practitioners in selecting appropriate machine learning models for the diagnosis of breast cancer to arrive at an early diagnosis and prevent poor outcomes.

articleTitle: TECHAID: AI-driven application for prognostic maintenance for mobile hardware using linear regression
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Smartphones have become essential tools for both personal and professional use, playing a critical role in maintaining efficient workflows across communication, productivity, and entertainment. However, as these devices grow more complex, hardware malfunctions can significantly disrupt their functionality. The “Repair of Computers and Communication Equipment” industry in the Philippines is projected to reach approximately 64.6 million USD by 2024 [1], reflecting a growing demand for smartphone repairs. However, a lack of intelligent diagnostic tools leaves users unaware of potential hardware defects until significant damage occurs, resulting in costly repairs and productivity losses. The purpose of this study is to predict mobile hardware and provide preventive measures. The researchers from Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) conducted the study using a purposive sample of 114 respondents. The study applied the ISO/IEC 25010 standard to evaluate the application’s functional suitability, usability, maintainability, and performance efficiency. The results demonstrated overall satisfaction across all evaluated categories: functional suitability scored a mean of 4.41, usability 4.34, and both maintainability and performance efficiency 4.37. The findings highlight the application’s effectiveness in delivering accurate diagnostics and preventive recommendations, offering significant value by reducing the impact of hardware failures on users.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of EBG structured high gain microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In order to improve important performance parameters like gain, directivity, and radiation characteristics, this work explores the use of electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures in microstrip patch antennas. Antenna efficiency is increased by suppressing surface waves and reducing backward radiation by adding EBG structures to the ground plane of the antenna. The study investigates the effects of several EBG designs on antenna performance, including square, swastika, crosshair, E-, S-, spiral, and L-shaped structures. A baseline Microstrip antenna without EBG, a single EBG element, a one- dimensional (1-D) array of EBG elements, and a two-dimensional (2-D) array of EBG elements are the four different design techniques used. Upon comparison, it is noticed that the L-shaped 3X3 EBG antenna exhibits high gain comparatively other structures. Using simulations, each configuration's gain, return loss (S11), and radiation patterns are examined.

articleTitle: The effect of tax knowledge, tax awareness, tax audit, and tax rates on individual taxpayer compliance in the digital era
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: As stated in the Law of the Republic of Indonesia Number 9 of 1994 which contains amendments to the Law of the Republic of Indonesia Number 6 of 1983, taxpayers are people with an income of at least 54 million per year or in the form of agencies (with the terms and conditions stated in the law). Every Indonesian citizen who is designated as a tax and has an NPWP is also required to report annual tax returns. Compliance with tax regulations is also a form of compliance with the 5th precept of Pancasila. Although it has been regulated in lawD this taxation obligation is also still experiencing fraud. Many people still violate or are reluctant to pay taxes because they are considered detrimental. This study uses a quantitative method with a questionnaire as a research instrument filled out by 100 respondents. The data were processed with SMART-PLS software with the SEM-PLS method to determine the path analysis. The results of this study state that tax knowledge (X1), tax compliance awareness (X2), and tax audits (X3) have a positive and significant effect on individual mandatory compliance. Tax rates (X4) have a significant negative effect on individual taxpayer compliance in the digital era. It can be concluded that a decrease in tax rates is fel t to increase individual compliance with taxes in this digital era.

articleTitle: Classification of random forest method on photovoltaic temperature and IoT monitoring for energy conversion
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In recent years, maximizing the energy conversion performance of photovoltaic (PV) systems has become increasingl y important, especially in the context of sustainable energy development. This study utilizes Internet of Things (IoT) technology and the Random Forest (RF) algorithm to optimize the performance monitoring of photovoltaic systems. IoT devices are used to collect real-time environmental and operational data, such as temperature, solar radiation, and system voltage, which affect PV performance. A classification method is applied to process this data and identify the most significant factors affecting energy conversion efficiency. By analyzing data patterns and classifying performance levels, the RF model helps predict optimal operating conditions and detect anomalies. This study shows that the combination of IoT-based monitoring and machine learning through Random Forest not only improves predictive maintenance of PV systems but can also improve energy conversion efficiency. The test results obtained Comparison of 20% and 30% Test Data in the Random Forest Algorithm are that the 20% Test Data provides the best accuracy of (90%) and the 30% Test Data is (87%). Then the sensor testing integrated with IoT is able to monitor voltage, current and power in energy conversion from PV.

articleTitle: Analysis and classification of tomato leaf disease using YOLOV8
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Diseases in tomato plants primarily affect the leaves, causing symptoms such as yellowing, wilting, and brown spots, which can impair photosynthesis and reduce crop yield. Tomato leaf diseases are often due to fungal or viral infections. Traditionally, these diseases are classified manually by observing leaf conditions directly, a method that is inefficient and limited by human expertise, especially at scale. This study leverages YOLOv8 for automated analysis and classification of diseases in tomato leaves. YOLOv8 represents a significant advancement in the YOLO series, providing faster and more precise detection compared to earlier versions. The best result of this research are 97.92% accuracy, 0.32 loss, 99.60% precision, 99.50% recall, 99.30% mAP50, and 92.80% mAP50-95.

articleTitle: Traffic control system modelling to control traffic lights using smart camera
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: An intelligent system enhances the current traffic light control system by detecting the number of vehicles at intersections, whether congested or not. Presently, the system identifies the number of vehicles and adjusts the green light duration to prioritize congested sides of an intersection. However, it is limited to capturing the number of vehicles stopping before the red light, unable to account for vehicles beyond the red light or measure vehicle speeds. Consequently, fast-moving vehicles may benefit from excess green light time, potentially increasing the risk of accidents. To address this issue, the DKI Jakarta Traffic Control System Management Unit implements a green light time limit to ensure equitable road usage at intersections. This approach, though effective, still falls short in managing congestion at specific critical points requiring advanced solutions. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a promising remedy, enabling the system to monitor vehicle speeds and predict traffic density before and after red lights. This study adopts a prototype model to simulate real-world conditions using toy cars and scaled road scenarios. The prototype integrates available tools and materials to create a traffic control system equipped with intelligen t traffic light management. Using the YOLOv8 algorithm, the prototype successfully detects vehicles waiting at red lights and measures the speed of approaching cars, paving the way for improved traffic regulation in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Evaluation of spectrum sliced-FSO communication system incorporating different modulation schemes
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In the radio-frequency (RF) spectrum, optical wireless communication (OWC) emerges as a promising alternative due to its high data capacity, immunity to electromagnetic interference, and enhanced security potential. This paper explores OWC networks using various modulation schemes, including Return-to-Zero (RZ), Non-Return-to-Zero (NRZ), and On-Off Keying (OOK). Simulation results, conducted via OptiSystem, reveal that bit rates of up to 40 Gb/s over distances up to 500 km are achievable. Maximum Q factors, minimum bit error rates (BER), and signal power across time and frequency spectra are analyzed and compared for each modulation scheme, highlighting OOK’s superior performance. The study examines the highest Q factors in relation to received power at varying distances up to 500km, signal interference by changing modulation format. Ultimately, this research aims to balance data efficiency and adaptability for OWC application by applying wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) system.

articleTitle: Low-cost hardware solution for PCM/FM telemetry data encoder based on IRIG-106 standard
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The PCM telemetry data encoder, part of the PCM/FM transmitter system used in rocket telemetry, follows the IRIG-106 standard. It collects data from sensors that monitor flight parameters like inertia, combustion pressure, and vibration. These encoders are usually developed by defense industries, with limited public details and a high cost of around $30,000 per unit or nearly 500 million rupiah in 2011. This paper presents a low-cost alternative using an STM32 microcontroller for under $30, capable of handling telemetry data at 1.024 Mbps. The hardware design was validated through a proof-of-concept using MATLAB Simulink and LTspice simulations and tested with a Zodiac TRFM02-S FM transmitter and Cortex RTR S-Band receiver. The test performance was compared with the Zodiac CMA, a telemetry encoder originally manufactured by Zodiac Data Systems and now produced by Safran, which also follows the IRIG-106 standard. Results showed no significant difference in BER between the two systems, although the low-cost solution had a slightly lower quality factor. It required a 1% loop bandwidth for similar performance, while the CMA only needed 0.3%. Despite this, the low-cost design is still effective for telemetry use, as it remains within the receiver’s maximum allowable loop bandwidth of 3%.

articleTitle: Dropout-integrated attention mechanism in CNN-LSTM prediction model for vehicle-mounted air quality monitoring
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The CNN-LSTM (Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory) model is widely used for urban air quality prediction; however, it often struggles from suboptimal accuracy due to its limited capacity to effectively capture complex spatial and temporal dependencies. To address this limitation, an attention mechanism was integrated into the CNN-LSTM model, enhancing its ability to focus on important features. However, this approach is still prone to overfitting, which compromises its generalization ability and accuracy in real-world applications. In this study, we propose the integration of dropout into the attention mechanism to enhance the CNN-LSTM model for vehicle-mounted air quality monitoring systems. The incorporation of a dropout-enhanced attention mechanism mitigates overfitting, further improving the model’s accuracy and generalization performance. Experimental results, based on real-world data collected from high-traffic urban areas, demonstrate that the Dropout Attention CNN-LSTM model outperforms both the baseline CNN-LSTM and the attention-enhanced CNN-LSTM models. Specifically, the enhanced model achieves a 6% increase in accuracy. The model also attains a precision of 95.1%, a recall of 94.2%, and an F1 score of 96.1%. These results underscore the model’s superior reliability and its suitability for real-time air quality monitoring in complex urban environments.

articleTitle: Meta learning for NOMA-MISO systems based full-duplex transmission
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The fast growth in wireless communication capacity demands adaptable systems that can control wireless resources efficiently to ensure a good and fair user experience. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) offer the opportunity to achieve modern communication goals. In this paper, wireless service is provided to several clients using a combination of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and multiple-input single-output (MISO) over a full-duplex (FD) channel. After using a pairing technique, the BS divides the coverage area into clusters is one suggested approach. Each cluster has only two users. Once everyone in a cluster is treated equally and their circumstances are considered, a sufficient amount of power is assigned to each of them using the NOMA technique. Feature engineering techniques are applied over the generated datasets to help the models find the pattern between the input datasets that leads to robust models. An examination and evaluation of the signal-to-interference-pulse-noise ratio (SINR), and the bit error rate (BER) attained for each user in the cluster in an acceptable value. Moreover, the potential throughput for strong user is maximized. To train different DL models controlled by one ML model to predict the optimal power allocation factor (PAF) that controlled transmitted power.

articleTitle: Fostering a proficient IoT workforce in Vietnam: obstacles and suggestions
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: To enhance its semiconductor sector, Vietnam must cultivate a proficient IoT workforce to ensure competitiveness. This study examines the difficulties and potential for the development of IoT human capital in Vietnam's semiconductor industry, employing mixed techniques that include data analysis and interviews with 20 experts. Research indicates discrepancies between existing IoT expertise and industrial requirements, including deficiencies in technical skills, insufficient collaboration between academia and industry, and a lack of soft skills. The report provides a framework for IoT workforce development through partnership among government, business, and academia to solve these concerns. Essential recommendations encompass integrating curriculum with international standards, cultivating collaborations, advocating for reskilling, recruiting global talent, and encouraging innovation. By carefully investing in IoT expertise, Vietnam may improve its competitiveness and secure a greater portion of the worldwide semiconductor industry, projected to reach USD 803 billion by 2028. As Vietnam advances towards Industry 4.0, a proficient IoT workforce will be essential for success in the transforming semiconductor sector.

articleTitle: Speak-up: web-based speech disorder detection system with recommended speech therapy for grade four and five elementary students using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Detecting speech disorders in children is challenging for existing tools as they rely on the resource-intensive assessments performed by Speech Language Pathologists (SLP). Similarly, speech therapy is often inaccessible and expensive, especially in rural communities. To address these concerns, the researchers developed the following: an automated acoustic feature extraction for both live and recorded audio input. Second, a web-based system that can classify normal and disordered speech namely articulation disorder, phonological disorder, and stuttering. Third, gamified speech therapy exercises that administer early interventions for children. Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), the model achieved 88% accuracy in identifying normal and disordered speech. Normal and stuttering achieved F1 scores of 93% and 91% respectively, while articulation and phonological disorders achieved F1 scores of 84%. Following the model’s integration into the web-based system, it was evaluated on 34 children with identified speech disorders. The model correctly identified stuttering with 81% accuracy, phonological and articulation disorders with 71% and 73% accuracy, respectively, for an overall accuracy of 75%. Furthermore, the researchers used the ISO 25010:2011 software quality standard to evaluate the system. The accumulated results were satisfactory in terms of functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, and reliability, with mean scores of 3.14 , 3.19, 3.10, and 3.14, respectively.

articleTitle: Impact of AI-powered business intelligence on smart city policy-making and data-driven governance
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Business Intelligence (BI) systems is revolutionizing the ways of governance in smart cities through data management, real-time analytics, and forecasting. These systems improve urban planning, resource allocation, and utilization, as well as, people and asset protection, and enhance transparency and responsibility. But barriers such as concerns about privacy, weaknesses of algorithms, and legal restrictions, prevent their widespread use. This paper considers the usage, benefits, and obstacles of AI-enabled BI tools in the governance of smart cities considering pressing issues such as integration with blockchain, Explainable AI (XAI), and IoT. Based on a comprehensive literature review, the research aims to highlight the usefulness of AI technologies in developing inclusive sustainable urban spaces.

articleTitle: Early fusion techniques for enhanced pneumonia detection in chest X-ray analysis
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Pneumonia, a significant global health concern, necessitates accurate diagnostic tools to enable timely and effective intervention. This study applies Early Fusion techniques to enhance pneumonia detection in chest X-ray analysis by integrating feature extraction methods—Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), and Local Binary Pattern (LBP). The fused features were used to train multiple machine learning models, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Neural Networks, and Support Vector Machines (SVM). Utilizing a dataset of 5,937 chest X-ray images, the SVM model achieved the highest accuracy (94.00%) and area under the curve (AUC) score (93.95%), demonstrating superior diagnostic performance compared to other models. The Early Fusion approach effectively captured complementary patterns in X-ray images, addressing challenges such as noise and subtle variability. These findings highlight the potential of fusion-based frameworks to improve diagnostic accuracy and reliability, supporting radiologists with automated tools for clinical decision-making. Future research will focus on validating the approach on larger, diverse datasets and improving the interpretability of fusion models while optimizing resource requirements to enable scalable deployment in real-world healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Synergizing AI and blockchain for efficient, transparent patient data management and secure online sharing
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a decentralized hospital records and image sharing platform on blockchain, integrating an Inter Planetary File System (IPFS) and AI-driven Feedback. Addressing the critical need for secure and efficient sharing of patient data and medical images in healthcare, the platform utilizes IPFS and blockchain technology to ensure the utmost security and tamper-proof storage. The user-friendly interface, built with React.js and Web3.js, enables seamless access and management of medical records. Smart contracts written in Solidity enhance security and transparency, providing an effective means for authorized sharing of medical records. The platform includes an AI feedback section for securely submitting feedback via smart contracts, with MetaMask ensuring secure interactions and offering valuable insights into healthcare management. The solution aims to revolutionize healthcare data sharing, prioritizing privacy, and improved patient outcomes. This comprehensive solution aims to revolutionize healthcare data sharing, ensuring privacy, security, and fostering improved patient outcomes. Leveraging K10 cross-validation, we evaluated the performance of our AI models, including Random Forest (RF), which demonstrated the highest accuracy at 92.5% ± 3.25% and an AUC of 0.925, with a critical value of p < 0.0001. Additional metrics including F1 Score, Sensitivity, and Specificity contribute to comprehensive assessment.

articleTitle: Electrical load forecasting for commercial buildings using LSTM based algorithms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Short term load forecasting is essential in commercial buildings for sourcing power where price is time sensitive. Other algorithms developed for aggregated load at utility companies level, produce inaccurate results for specific bulk consumers like shopping malls, airports, universities etc. This paper presents a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network combined with a fully connected layer architecture for short-term load forecasting (STLF). In this approach, after preprocessing the time series historical data, a new set of features are generated by lagging external weather variables and historical load values to capture temporal patterns. To fully assess our model’s performance in STLF, we conduct load forecasts for three short-term windows:one-hour-ahead,one-day-aheadandone-week-aheadforecasts. The performance of the proposed architecture is benchmarked against widely used models. The proposed model outperformed the baseline models by at least 7%, 9.37%, and 12.4% in MAE (Mean Absolute Error), MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), and RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error), respectively, for the one-week-ahead forecast. Similarly, it surpassed the baseline models by at least 9% in the one-day-ahead forecast and by at least 5% in the one-hour-ahead forecast across all metrics.

articleTitle: Smart IoT-integrated weather analytics system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes an IoT-based weather monitoring system utilizing Raspberry Pi 4 Model B as the core component to collect extensive weather data, including ambient temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, altitude, rainwater, ultraviolet rays, and ambient light intensity, utilizing appropriate sensors. A contemporary, user-friendly website serves as the interface, offering functionalities such as real-time data visualization and email notifications. The paper begins with an overview of the IoT and weather monitoring domains to underscore their importance and the necessity for advancements in these fields. A comprehensive literature review is conducted to identify trends, achievements, and existing gaps in previous IoT-based weather monitoring research. Following this, a detailed design strategy is outlined, covering all development phases from initial planning to final execution. This design framework is applied during the implementation phase, where the system's development and testing processes are meticulously recorded and analyzed. The results section provides an in-depth analysis of the collected data and evaluates the system's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability. The paper concludes with a summary of key findings, discussing the contributions to the field, identifying limitations, and proposing recommendations for future improvements and extensions to enhance the system's capabilities, thus addressing the gaps identified in the literature review.

articleTitle: BEYOND THE ARCH: a web and mobile alumni record verification system for the University of Santo Tomas Office of the Registrar
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: BEYOND THE ARCH: A Web and Mobile Alumni Record Verification System marks a transformative shift in alumni verification processes at the University of Santo Tomas’ Office of the Registrar. Traditionally manual and time-consuming, the current process faced significant bottlenecks during the 2021 pandemic. This system integrated features like document scanning, automated ticketing, certificate generation, key personnel info cataloguing, user account management, event calendaring, and analytics for performance monitoring. These features significantly enhanced efficiency, accuracy, and transparency in alumni records verification, curbing fraudulent claims and fake credentials. While human intervention may still be necessary for cross-checking, result accuracy, and data privacy compliance, the system's integration with the existing alumni database from 2004 onwards, combined with partial automation, augments efficiency and security. It addresses a critical gap in the Philippines, lacking a centralised clearinghouse for alumni records. Employing the iterative waterfall methodology ensured structured development and flexibility, validated through unit and user acceptance testing. Its successful design and implementation hav e streamlined request management and tracking, improving response times, user satisfaction, and reducing administrative workload. Recommendations for future enhancements include extending verification capabilities, enhancing document scanning accuracy, refining filtering, sorting, and search functionalities, and integrating Senior High School records, among other enhancements.

articleTitle: Low-speed flow oscillations in a cavity with slanted front and aft walls
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: An experimental study was performed to examine the effects of slanted aft and front walls on cavity flow dynamics. Experiments were conducted at a free-stream velocity of 26 m/s using a cavity with a length-to-depth ratio of 3. Unsteady and time-averaged pressure measurements across the cavity span were used to assess the impact of slant angles of 15°, 30°, and 45° on the frequency spectra, with a rectangular cavity serving as a baseline. The baseline case showed dominant oscillation frequencies in line with Rossiter’s feedback mechanism. For the 15° slant angle, cavity oscillation frequencies were present but with reduced amplitudes and deviations from Rossiter’s equation. At a 30° slant angle, the spectra revealed a broadband peak of high amplitude, whereas the 45° slant angle suppressed oscillation peaks, indicating the absence of the feedback mechanism. Noise analysis indicated that the overall noise was highest for the 30° case, lower for the 45° case, and similar to the baseline for the 15° slant angle, with a slight increase noticed near the leading edge. The results underscore the role of slant angle in modulating cavity oscillations and noise, suggesting that the 30° cavity may be better suited for broadband energy harvesting due to its broad frequency response.

articleTitle: Steel defects classification based on vision attention
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Steel surface defects are imperfections or irregularities that arise during the production, processing, or finishing of steel products. Surface defects degrade the robustness and stability of steel, compromise its structural integrity. As steel is a widely -used material across the industries, the quality assurance of steel is extremely important. Traditional defect detection methods are prone to human errors and difficult to detect small or subtle defects. Deep learning offers a promising solution in automated defect detection and classification, especially Vision Transformer. This paper implements different pre-trained deep learning models to classify steel surface defects from NEU dataset. The Vision Transformer has the best performance with the highest classification accuracy of 99.17% and the least computation time of 229s. Vision Transformer successfully capture the complex patterns in steel defects and being able to classify them accurately with the powerful attention mechanism.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a low-cost single-ended primary-inductor converter (SEPIC) for enhanced maximum power point tracking in a photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study presents the implementation of a Single-ended Primary-inductor Converter (SEPIC) converter-based maximum power point tracker (MPPT) in a photovoltaic (PV) system. The SEPIC converter, known for its wide operating range and non - inverted output, presents a suitable option as a DC-DC converter interface between the PV array and load. A modified Incremental Conductance (IC) algorithm is implemented on dSPACE DS1104 controller board based on 50 kHz PWM to perform global MPP tracking. The purpose of the modification is to allow the IC algorithm to converge to the global maximum power point under partial shading conditions by initializing the algorithm near the estimated global peak. For performance verification, the setup is extensively tested using an indoor PV emulator under static and dynamic conditions. Under partial shading conditions, its performance was benchmarked against the conventional IC algorithm. Results indicate that the prototype achieves efficiency of over 98% in both static and dynamic tests for EN50530-defined c-Si and thin film modules. On boot-up, the tracker can locate the maximum power point within 2-3 seconds. This study addresses the need for cost-effective MPPT solutions to maximise PV energy extraction under dynamic and partial shading conditions, leveraging SEPIC converter versatility to enhance performance and accessibility.

articleTitle: A clustering model for data transmission based on deep learning for energy efficiency enhancement in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are intensively explored because they can collect and analyze data in numerous applications. However, sensor nodes' limited energy resources hinder network durability. We propo se using Deep Learning-based Grouping Model Approach (DL-GMA) to reduce energy consumption in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Advanced deep learning approaches like Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) optimize cluster formation, select Cluster Heads (CH), and maintain them to increase energy efficiency in DL-GMA. Energy Efficiency (88.7%), Network Stability (90.8%), Network Scalability (87.1%), Congestion Level (18.3%), and Quality of Service (QoS) (93.4%) show that DL-GMA optimises energy consumption and improves network performance. Deep learning and intelligent grouping lengthen WSN lifespan and enhance data transmission efficiency in our solution. DL-GMA improves wireless sensor network energy optimization by increasing data transmission efficiency and resolving energy resource constraints.

articleTitle: An IoT-based smart farming solution for sustainable agriculture: integrating AI, cloud computing, and 4G communication for enhanced productivity
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive smart farming solution designed to address the limitations of current systems and the practical needs of modern farmers. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies such as the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), and cloud computing, our solution aims to improve agricultural productivity and sustainability. By integrating industrial-grade sensors with a user-friendly software platform, our system facilitates transparent monitoring and control of agricultural conditions at various scales, while also providing tools for efficient farm finance management. The star topology architecture, combined with 4G network communication, ensures system reliability and efficient data transmission. AI integration provides insights and actionable recommendations, allowing farmers to effectively optimize crop yields and resource utilization. Our approach addresses significant shortcomings observed in existing smart agriculture projects, such as outdated communication technology, limited scalability, and inadequate user interfaces for data management. By integrating solar power to power the system and emphasizing user-centric design, our solution promotes environmental sustainability and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Government product recommendation systems in e-Katalog: leveraging large language models with retrieval-augmented generation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Indonesia's electronic catalog (e-Katalog) is a platform developed to facilitate government procurement, providing an extensive collection of products and services that simplifies purchasing processes, enhances transparency, and reduces costs. However, the exponential growth in the number of listed products has led to challenges such as information overload, complicating the selection process for buyers. E-katalog lacks the ability to effectively deliver personalized, context-aware recommendations that could further support procurement strategies. To address these challenges, this research aims to develop a product recommendation system for e-Katalog using large language models (LLMs) integrated with the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework. The goal is to provide contextual and relevant recommendations, prioritizing MSMEs and local products to support effective procurement decision-making by government institutions. This study compares three embedding models all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-distilroberta-v1, and all-mpnet-base-v2, based on their effectiveness in product retrieval, with all-mpnet-base-v2 achieving the highest average similarity score of 0.72. This enabled the RAG-based system, powered by GPT-3.5 Turbo, to deliver more targeted and meaningful product suggestions, thereby effectively promoting local products and MSMEs.

articleTitle: Review of machine learning-based techniques for detecting specific and general objects
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In recent years, machine learning has become an essential technology across multiple areas, particularly in object detection systems, where it enhances accuracy and automation. This paper critically examines the object detection techniques developed between 2020 and 2024, focusing on three popular methods, namely You Only Look Once (YOLO), Single Shot Detector (SSD) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). These architectures have been assessed based on their performance in different implementation environments, highlighting strengths and limitations. Further, the architectural layers of each model are discussed to offer deep insights into their operational mechanisms. YOLO, known for its fast inference speed and adaptability, is particularly suited for real-time surveillance and autonomous navigation applications. Specialized models such as Fuzzy C-Means are also explored for their advantages in object segmentation, tracking and multi-object detection. The paper concludes by examining the future direction of object detection, emphasizing the need for more efficient and adaptable models to integrate machine learning into everyday applications.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of knowledge distillation models using the knowledge retention score
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In this study, we introduce the Knowledge Retention Score (KRS) as a universal performance metric to evaluate knowledge distillation (KD) models. Unlike traditional evaluation methods that focus solely on final accuracy, KRS captures both intermediate feature alignment and output consistency between teacher and student models. This dual-component metric, combining feature similarity and output agreement, provides a comprehensive understanding of knowledge transfer effectiveness. We applied KRS across various KD techniques, teacher-student network pairs, and tasks, including image classification, object detection, and image segmentation, using multiple datasets such as CIFAR-100, COCO, and Oxford-IIIT Pet. The results revealed that feature-based KD methods achieved higher KRS in object detection tasks, indicating superior knowledge retention. In contrast, relational-based KD performed well in image segmentation but did not surpass feature-based KD. Response-based KD showed the lowest KRS, particularly in image classification tasks. The findings validate KRS as a robust and consistent metric, offering insights into the efficiency and effectiveness of different KD strategies across diver se contexts. This study sets the groundwork for future benchmarking and optimization of KD models using KRS, advancing the field of model compression and deployment on resource-constrained devices.

articleTitle: Harnessing AI for agriculture utilizing color-condition camera sensors and thermal imaging drones for crop color-condition detection and predictive yield analysis with inventory management system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)

authors.preferredName: Cris Ariel Antwaun Rolando C. Sison

abstract: Technological Gaps and Challenges for Agriculture in the Philippines Such advancements may be relevant to other countries as well but we should also consider that there is greater potential of technology adoption with these purposes than ever befo re, especially those small-scale farmers from local areas who have less accessibility on technological trendsetting. In this study, we attempt to solve these problems using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in order to improve crop monitoring and predictive yiel d amidst the climate change. Color-condition detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with 76.97% accuracy and predictive analysis by Artificial Neural Network(ANN). This optimizes the timing of planting and harvest, depending on the combination of these algorithms. This study aims to capture the crops’ maturity through color-condition detection and gather data for yield analysis by capturing the thermal temperature of the soil. The AI can identify crop health and maturity issues, such as nutrient deficiencies. It will also enhance crop yield predictions by inputting information such as soil types, temperature, fertilizers used, and weather conditions. Additionally, this study implements a partial website system to serve as an interface for the images captured by the camera attached to the drone. This website also showcases the goals of the proposed study. Furthermore, it includes a crop stock and inventory management feature to reduce paper usage and promote an eco-friendly environment. Through this innovation, local farmers can adapt to new technologies, improve farm productivity, reduce crop wastage, and strengthen their ability to meet market demands while promoting sustainable practices.

articleTitle: Real-time object detection on DJI Ryze Tello quadrotor drone with YOLO and SSD algorithms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Drones equipped with real-time object detection offer a novel perspective on our environment, yet they encounter challenges related to hardware limitations and the demands of complex applications. These challenges necessitate innovative solutions, particularly given the potential benefits in areas such as search and rescue operations, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, and environmental conservation. This study investigates the feasibility of real-time object recognition on the DJI Ryze Tello drone using two advanced algorithms: YOLOv3 and Single Shot Multibox Detector (SSD). The evaluation of these algorithms focuses on three key metrics: accuracy, processing speed, and resource consumption. Experiments were carried out in a controlled indoor setting and in the field, with changing lighting as well as background complexity. The results showed that SSD outperformed YOLOv3 in precision, recall, and F1-Score (60-70%), making it more suitable for accuracy-focused applications. In contrast, YOLOv3’s faster processing speed (50-60 FPS) is better suited for scenarios requiring quick decision-making. This research offers valuable guidance for selecting these models based on specific application needs, particularly in agriculture, search and rescue, and surveillance.

articleTitle: Advancements in computer vision-based assistive technologies for visually impaired
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: The advancement of assistive technologies for visually impaired individuals has seen significant strides, leveraging the power of computer vision-based object recognition and detection. This literature review explores various approaches aimed at enhancing navigation, obstacle detection, and overall mobility for the visually impaired. By utilizing methods such as real-time object detection, deep learning algorithms, and wearable devices, these technologies convert visual information into comprehensible formats through image-to-text and text-to-speech processes. Recent research efforts have focused on integrating these technologies to provide real- time auditory feedback, thereby enhancing spatial awareness and safety. For instance, mobile applications like "Smart_Eye" and wearable devices based on platforms such as Raspberry Pi employ advanced sensors and machine learning to identify and describ e objects, providing crucial auditory cues to users. Systematic reviews of wearable electronic aids and technologically advanced guidance systems underline the importance of consistent detection accuracy and user adaptability. Despite the promising developments, challenges such as spatial biases, computational intensity, and user interface complexities remain. This review consolidates the findings from various studies, presenting methods used, limitations encountered, and the potential impact of computer vision-based recognition systems to assist visually impaired users. By converting image data to textual descriptions and subsequently into speech, these technologies offer comprehensive support, significantly improving the independence and qualit y of life for visually impaired individuals. Overall, the integration of computer vision, deep learning, and real-time feedback systems marks a transformative phase in assistive technology, providing visually impaired individuals with enhanced tools to navigate and interact with their environments effectively.

articleTitle: A review of machine learning and drone-based solar panel inspection techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper aims to improve defect identification, operational efficiency, and cost-effectiveness of drone-based photovoltaic (PV) solar panel inspection methods by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms and modern imaging technologies. As the usage of renewable energy sources develops, it is vital to maintain solar panels in a timely and accurate way to guarantee their maximum perfor- mance. Innovative methods for large-scale solar panel inspection are made possible by drones equipped with thermal imaging, YOLOv8 object detection, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Single Shot Multibox Detectors (SSD), and mapping tools like Pix4D. Every method has proven effective in locating flaws, including hotspots, dust buildup, and cracks, enhancing system performance. This study thoroughly analyses these techniques, evaluating their feasibility, accuracy, and efficiency for small and large-scale solar installations. We hope to provide insights into the best drone-based solutions for solar panel inspection and maintenance by contrasting the advantages and disadvantages of each strategy, thereby assisting in developing a more dependable and sustainable renewable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Bibliometric review of smart sensor for health monitoring
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Smart sensors and medical health technologies are becoming increasingly popular due to their potential for real-time, non-invasive health monitoring and diagnostics. With the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), these devices can track vital signs and important biomarkers, supporting the management of chronic diseases. This study employs bibliometric analysis using tools like VOSviewer to map research trends in this domain, identifying collaborations, emerging keywords, and contributions from institutions and countries. Findings indicate a significant increase in publications and citations, especially after 2010, highlighting influential journals such as IEEE Sensors Journal. The primary focus is on health monitoring applications and advancements in sensor technology, with an increasing use of terms like "machine learning" and "data analytics." These findings provide insights into future research directions and technological innovations that impact medical health applications. It is recommended that future development integrate advanced data processing techniques and apply sensors in infrastructure and smart city environments, aiming to create systems that are more responsive, efficient, and sustainable.

articleTitle: Design and evaluation of different screens in a wind tunnel for flow management
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Honeycombs and screens placed within a wind tunnel system contribute to enhancing flow quality. This paper analyses the effects of screens on flow within the wind tunnel system, utilising an axial flow fan as the testing device. The design of various screen samples will be executed, and a graphical simulation of how these screens will function will be performed using the SolidWorks 2022 software. Following this, the designs will be 3D printed for physical testing. The designed screen samples will have varying wire lengths and aperture lengths while maintaining the same mesh extruded thickness and total diameter. Recently, the hexagonal mesh type is more likely to be used for designing screens within a wind tunnel system. In this study, the best-performing screen type is the circular mesh sample 5 with a 5.16% decrease in Reynolds number, followed by hexagonal mesh sample 2 with a 4.96% decrease, and lastly, the square mesh sample 5 with a 4.83% decrease in Reynolds number. The designed screens in this study validated the open literature that improved screens will also reduce turbulence and foster good flow quality, which can be used for testing within a wind tunnel system.

articleTitle: The impact of foliar fertiliser on oil palm trees using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Agriculture has undergone a significant transformation from traditional to modern practices, incorporating advanced technologies to enhance productivity and sustainability. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of foliar spraying for nutrient supplementation on oil palms using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Specifically, this research employs UAVs for nutrient spraying and multispectral mapping. The fertiliser aerial deployments were carried out monthly while the multispectral data captures were done thrice in between these intervals. Findings indicate that the use of foliar fertilisation method via UAVs yields better results over time, as evidenced by the analysis of temporal changes in the Leaf Chlorophyll Index. This suggest s that UAV-assisted foliar spraying can be a more efficient and effective approach for nutrient supplementation in oil palm cultivation. Additionally, this paper highlights two primary advantages: (i) the use of UAVs for agricultural spraying, and (ii) the use of UAVs for assessing chlorophyll content. The latter offers a non-destructive alternative to traditional laboratory methods for measuring nitrogen (N) levels, enabling scientists and agronomists to evaluate crop performance constructively.

articleTitle: PLANTery: an IoT-based automated plant watering system and pest detection using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This study addresses busy individual’s challenges in maintaining plants, specifically watering and pest control. PLANTery automates plant care by using IoT sensors (for soil moisture, temperature, and humidity) to activate irrigation as needed and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for real-time pest detection, alerting users, and recommending anti-pest measures. The system received an excellent rating from respondents, with an overall weighted mean of 4.74, indicating high functionality, efficiency, reliability, and usability. This result reflects intense user satisfaction and demonstrates that the system effectively achieves its objectives, providing robust solutions for plant care.

articleTitle: Mental health evaluation during internet blackouts: a machine learning approach
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Internet has become essential for modern communication and access to services. However, blackouts during politically sensitive periods can disrupt daily life, causing anxiety and distress. This study examines the psychological effects of internet black outs during the Bangladesh Quota Movement in July 2024, when internet access was shutdown to control information flow. The disruption significantly affected communication, financial transactions, and access to essential services, exacerbating anxiety, stress, tension, and feelings of isolation among citizens. A survey of 980 participants with 20 questions assessed behavioral, emotional, and psychological impacts. Results showed stress levels ranging from minimal to extreme, reflecting widespread distress. The study also used machine learning models to predict stress levels. The Decision Tree model showed limited predictive power, with around 55% accuracy, while the Random Forest model improved to 67%. XGBoost performed better than both, achieving over 94% in all metrics, demonstrating better accuracy. These findings highlight the potential of advanced algorithms to model mental health impacts, enabling policymakers to develop targeted interventions and allocate resources efficiently, ultimately minimizing the psychological toll of future internet disruptions and improving overall preparedness.

articleTitle: Enhanced lathe tool positioning through wavelet-based image denoising techniques
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: Precise tool placement is crucial in smart manufacturing and automation. In micro-machining, tiny measurements must be very accurate. Finding edges accurately is a key step for good positioning and micrometer-level measurements. Image denoising was necessary before applying edge detection algorithms to enhance edge detection accuracy. Conventional filtering methods can be employed for denoising, but the work here investigates wavelet thresholding benefits in analyzing multiple resolutions and achieving better accuracy. An in-depth assessment of the quality of the denoised images is conducted. The quantitative analysis is done using metrics such as PSNR (peak signal to noise ratio), SSIM (structural similarity index measurement), MSE (mean squar e error) and others factors in which the wavelet based denoising method's results are compared at different scales. The results from the analysis show that the db1 wavelet based on SURE denoising method can efficiently remove a lot of Gaussian noise and restore the image details and data than Coiflets and Symlets wavelet techniques.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a portable low-cost internet-enabledI-Vcurve tracer utilizing Ćuk Converter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This work presents the development of an internet-enabled current-voltage (I-V) curve tracer prototype circuit. With an emphasis on cost-effectiveness and data accessibility, the prototype was constructed utilizing Raspberry Pi 4 as the data acquisition board equipped with a TFT display and webserver connectivity. The prototype was designed to handle up to 60V open-circuit voltage, 10A short-circuit current and a maximum power point of 250W. The measured data is processed programmatically with a filtering algorithm to smoothen the curve by removing outlier values measured due to noise. Further refinement was achieved by averaging multiple data points recorded at each step of a single duty cycle change. The prototype was tested on three commercially available PV modules through Chroma 62100H-600HS Solar Array Simulator. The proposed device achieved an overall average RMSE and RRMSE of 0.2848A and 6.4985% respectively. By combining linear duty cycle with linear gain changes across different regions of the I-V curve, a more even distribution of data points was achieved, resulting in a total scan time of 6.8 seconds. While sufficient for less accuracy-intensive tasks, the current prototype is not ideal for research-grade applications. It is expected that with the use of a dedicated printed circuit board (PCB), for reduced noise and enhanced signal integrity, higher accuracy could be achieved. Nonetheless, this project successfully demonstrated the feasibility of incorporating internet connectivity for remote monitoring of PV module status.

articleTitle: AI Jurist: empowering legal knowledge and practices in India
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In the field of legal studies and other related fields, identifying and to study accurate legal information, such as laws and case precedents, is a difficult challenge. The primary focus of this research is to utilise Natural Language Processing (NLP) and AI techniques for Legal Information Retrieval System to solve this challenge. This system will help lawyers and legal practitioners in building strong arguments, developing effective strategies, and making well-informed decisions critical for successful judicial proceedings. Additionally, it empowers individuals, even without prior legal expertise, to enhance their legal knowledge and better understand the law. Our study used a dataset of 70 thousand records where each record comprises case titles, proceedings, authors, citations, and legal related information. The input options for the system are either legal documents like FIRs or Query containing legal questions in the format of PDFs or Images. Afterwards, utilising the capabilities of LLMs the output is a detailed structured Legal Research Report that consists of prior cases, judgements, laws, courts etc. The system will exponentially boost efficiency by providing precise, time-saving, and easily accessible information with enhanced retrieval accuracy. The evaluation metrics yielded an 80% accuracy in quantitative evaluations, complemented by positive feedback from legal professionals highlighting the system's efficacy in delivering accurate, comprehensive, and relevant legal research reports. These results showcase the potential of proposed solution for practical implementation and further evaluations for its use in the legal domain. The proposed system has the capability to be a companion to humans in information gathering and understanding, thereby contributing towards the improvement of legal knowledge, legal research and the decision-making process.

articleTitle: HiSkul: a website for Florentino Torres high school with virtual walkthrough and chatbot
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: In the current digital landscape, education is vital for shaping both individuals and societies. This capstone project presents "HiSkul: A Website for Florentino Torres High School featuring a Virtual Walkthrough and Chatbot," designed to tackle several pressing challenges at the school. These challenges include a cumbersome admission process, insufficient real-time communication, and the lack of physical school tours for prospective students and their families. The HiSkul website offers a virtual walkthrough that creates an engaging experience, allowing users to explore the school's environment in a more interactive manner rather than relying solely on static images. Furthermore, the integrated chatbot serves as a valuable resource, enabli ng seamless communication among students, parents, teachers, and administrators by addressing questions about the school's programs, admission processes, and extracurricular options. This platform significantly enhances accessibility, allowing students and parents to easily gather information and make informed choices from home. The study identified key issues, including the overwhelming volume of daily admission inquiries, which can lead to the school administration losing track of applicants and available spaces. Additionally, the absence of real-time communication restricts opportunities for collaboration and feedback, while the lack of physical tours means potential students cannot fully experience the school's facilities.

articleTitle: Secure smart vision: intelligent object recognition system for visually impaired
publicationTitle: International Conference on Green Energy, Computing and Intelligent Technology 2024 (GEn-CITy 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a novel solution aimed at addressing the functional limitations experienced by visually impaired individuals through the development of a secure smart assistive device. It identifies and resolves common challenges such as object recognition, identification of packaged goods, currency coins and notes, text reading, and facial recognition encountered by this community. The proposed solution comprises an augmented reality wearable spectacle integrated with a smart vision system worn on the head. The spectacle is equipped with essential components including a camera, earphones, GPS module, and Internet connectivity (Wi-Fi & 4G) to enable real-time visual assistance. Meanwhile, the smart vision system features ultrasonic and IR sensors designed to detect objects in proximity and notify the user through vibrations. Seamless synchronization between the devices is achieved via Bluetooth connectivity, ensuring coordinated operation. The assistive device provides audible signals through earphones, enhancing usability for visually impaired individuals. Leveraging advanced Computer Vision techniques supported by OpenCV and Google Cloud Vision API, this research aims to deliver comprehensive support to the visually impaired community while ensuring security and reliability of the smart assistive device.
